data.title: Field
data.tagline: A field is one standalone piece of information in a record, such as client name, amount, or date.
data.learningOutcome: You can split "what to record" into a named field list, and tell fields apart from input controls and the form as a whole.
data.description: One client quote consists of four fields: client name, amount, status, and date. Before building a tool, splitting "what I want to record" into a field list matters more than sketching pages: the list drives the form, the list view, and validation. The field is the information itself; the input is just the control for filling it in.

learning.assumes: You have filled in web forms and seen the label above each input.
learning.outcome: You can split "what to record" into a named field list, and tell fields apart from input controls and the form as a whole.

distinctions.label: Input
distinctions.explanation: Input is the control used to type a field's value; Field is the piece of information itself.

distinctions.label: Data type
distinctions.explanation: Field answers "what to record"; Data Type answers "what format that information takes".

explanation.title: Fields drive the form
explanation.text: Each input on the form maps to one field. Four fields means the create page asks for exactly four things.

explanation.title: Fields drive the list
explanation.text: Each column in the list is a field. Whatever you will search by later should be a field now.

explanation.title: Fields drive validation
explanation.text: Amount must be a number, date must be pickable—validation follows the field, not the page.

data.boundary: The field is the information itself, the input is the control for entering it, and the form is the interface for a group of fields—three different layers. A field name answers "what to record" while a data type answers "what format"—also two different things. Prefer fewer fields first: every added field grows the form, the list, validation, and the mobile layout.

lessonPractice.title: While designing a quote tool, which of these is a field?

options.label: The "amount" of each quote
options.feedback: Correct. Amount is one standalone piece of information per record; client name, date, and status are fields too.

options.label: The "save" button at the bottom of the form
options.feedback: A button is an action entry, not recorded information. A field is the information itself, not the control.

options.label: The entire new-quote form
options.feedback: The form is the interface for filling in a group of fields; a field is one item inside it.

data.agentPrompt: Keep the quote tool to four fields for now: client name, amount, date, and status. Name and amount are required, date uses a date picker, status picks from "following up / won / archived." Do not add other fields yet.
